Effective dose estimation

Source: R/ed.R
ed.Rd

Estimates effective doses (ED p, e.g. ED50 or EC50) of fitted dose-response curves, for one or several curves, with standard errors by the delta method; confidence intervals follow with confint. Not available for fits in the BMD parameterisation (bmdpar of drmTMB).

Usage

ed(
  x,
  respLev = 50,
  linfct = NULL,
  newdata = NULL,
  random = TRUE,
  residual = FALSE,
  type = c("relative", "absolute"),
  vcov. = NULL
)

Arguments

x

a drmTMB object

respLev

effective dose level in percent, default is 50. The effective dose ED p is the dose at which the response has changed by p percent of the difference between the asymptote at low doses (the control) and the asymptote at high doses; for the hormesis models, the dose above the peak of the stimulation, see Details. For type="absolute", values of the response.

linfct

a matrix of linear functions to identify the parameters of the dose-response curve, with 5 rows (b1-b5) and one column for each model coefficient, or a list of such matrices; default is the identity matrix, which only works without covariates in fform; otherwise give newdata. Each matrix is paired with an entry of respLev.

newdata

a data frame with the values of the covariates in fform, one row for each dose-response curve, as an alternative to linfct; the dose is not needed. With grouping variables of the random effects, the curves of fitted groups, see Details. The effective doses are computed at each level of respLev for each row, named by the covariate and group values (or by the row names of newdata, if set).

random

logical. TRUE (default): rows of newdata with a fitted group give the effective dose of the curve of that group; for the other random effect terms, the standard errors include the variance of the random effects, i.e. they describe the effective dose of a new, randomly drawn group. FALSE: the effective doses of the population curve (random effects at zero), with the uncertainty of the fixed effects only; profile and bootstrap intervals need FALSE (or fitted groups). Without random effects, TRUE and FALSE are the same.

residual

logical, if TRUE, the residual variance is included in the standard error, for the dose at which a single new observation reaches the response level; gaussian family only, and not with a curvelink or a variance function

type

"relative" (default) for effective doses relative to the asymptotes, or "absolute" for the doses at which the curves reach the responses in respLev, on the scale of the response (proportions for binomial, beta-binomial and beta). Absolute effective doses depend on the asymptotes, and on their random effects; responses outside the range of a curve give NA, with a warning. The exponential and power models, without an upper asymptote, have absolute effective doses only.

vcov.

the covariance of the estimated parameters for the standard errors: a matrix as vcov() of the fit, or a function of the fit that returns one, e.g. the sandwich covariance vcovrobust; NULL (default) for vcov() of the fit. confint.edTMB then gives Wald intervals by default.

Value

An object of class edTMB, a list with the estimates (estimates), their covariance matrix (variance), the fit and the linear functions of the curves. The entries are named "level:curve", e.g. "50:lf1" or "50:time=24h", and "y=value:curve" for absolute effective doses. Use coef, vcov and confint, see edTMB-methods.

Details

Without random effects, or with random=FALSE, the effective doses are those of the population curves, with all random effects at zero, and their standard errors include the uncertainty of the fixed effects only. With random=TRUE, the standard errors also include the variance of the random effects, the variation of the effective dose between groups.

If a row of newdata gives a level of a grouping factor that is in the fitted data, the effective dose of that row is for the curve of the group, with its predicted random effects (the conditional modes), as in predict.drmTMB. These are shrunken towards the population curve, more so for groups with few observations. Their standard errors include the uncertainty of the fixed effects and the prediction error of the random effects, from the joint precision matrix of sdreport. Random effect terms without a grouping variable in newdata, or with a level that is not in the fitted data, are treated as above. Profile intervals are not available for the effective doses of fitted groups, see confint.edTMB.

For the hormesis models braincousens and cedergreen, the effective dose ED p is the dose above the peak of the stimulation at which the response has decreased from the response at dose zero (b2) by p percent of the difference to the lower asymptote b1, as in drc; with type="absolute", the dose above the peak at which the curve reaches the response. It has no closed form: it is found numerically, and its derivatives, for the standard errors, follow from the implicit function theorem. The models need a decreasing curve, with b3 < 0. With respLev=0, the effective dose is the dose above the peak at which the response returns to the response at dose zero, the limit of the stimulation (the zero equivalent point); see peak for the peak itself.

The effective dose ED p is relative to the range between the asymptotes, whereas the relative BMD of bmd (def="relative") is relative to the response at dose zero; they coincide only for a lower asymptote of 0. For the event family, the relative effective dose is the time by which p percent of the units with an event have had it (b2 is the proportion with an event); the time by which a proportion q of all units has had an event is given by type="absolute" with respLev = q.

See also

confint.edTMB, profile.edTMB, bootstrap, edTMB-methods, peak, bmd

Examples

mod <- drmTMB(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, model = "loglogistic",
              start = c(b1 = 0, b5 = 0), fix = c(b1 = TRUE, b5 = TRUE))
# ED10, ED50 and ED90, with profile likelihood intervals
(e <- ed(mod, respLev = c(10, 50, 90)))
#> Effective dose estimates:
#> 
#>        Estimate Std.Error
#> 10:lf1     1.34     0.189
#> 50:lf1     3.26     0.196
#> 90:lf1     7.94     1.055
confint(e)
#> Computing profile confidence intervals ...
#>            2.5 %    97.5 %
#> 10:lf1 0.9813186  1.774243
#> 50:lf1 2.8791625  3.703885
#> 90:lf1 6.1400175 10.652850
# doses at which the root length is 2 and 4 cm
ed(mod, respLev = c(2, 4), type = "absolute")
#> Effective dose estimates:
#> 
#>         Estimate Std.Error
#> y=2:lf1     5.04     0.414
#> y=4:lf1     3.22     0.173

# effective doses of several curves, given by the covariates in newdata
dmod <- drmTMB(cbind(no, total - no) ~ dose, data = daphnids, model = "loglogistic",
               family = "binomial", fform = b3 + b4 ~ 0 + time,
               start = c(b1 = 0, b2 = 1, b4 = 1000, b5 = 0),
               fix = c(b1 = TRUE, b2 = TRUE, b5 = TRUE))
ed(dmod, respLev = 50, newdata = data.frame(time = c("24h", "48h")))
#> Effective dose estimates:
#> 
#>             Estimate Std.Error
#> 50:time=24h     5134      1057
#> 50:time=48h     1509       188
